review_candidates.title: Account Manager
review_candidates.description: About Cartify Cartify is a B2B ordering platform for food and beverage. Restaurants order from their own suppliers in one place, with prices, order history and confirmations in writing instead of scattered across WhatsApp and phone calls. Cartify is the platform, not the supplier. Suppliers set their own prices, terms and deliveries. Cartify never takes title to the goods and never sits inside the commercial terms between a supplier and a restaurant. Team of eight, working out of Beirut. What you will do Sales signs the account. You are the reason it works. The portfolio is mixed by design: you will hold supplier accounts and restaurant accounts at the same time, and a good part of the value of the job is that you see both ends of the same order. Onboard suppliers properly the first time Own each new supplier from the day the agreement is signed to the day their first order comes through the platform. Collect the catalogue in usable form: item name, pack size, unit of measure, barcode, VAT treatment and the supplier's own SKU. The supplier's SKU and barcode are what appear on the purchase order, so an item entered wrong is an order that arrives wrong. Sit with the supplier while the price list is loaded and check it against the document they sent, line by line on the items that matter. Catalogues arrive in every format from a clean spreadsheet to a photograph of a printed sheet, and turning that into something the platform can hold is your work, not the supplier's. Refuse what cannot go live as submitted: no barcode, unclear pack size, or an item sold to order rather than from stock. Flag it and get the answer in writing rather than guessing. Set up and train the users who will actually work the account, meaning the sales rep who accepts the order, not only the owner who signed. Onboard restaurants so they order twice Set up the buyer's account, users and approval flow, and confirm their own suppliers are live before the first order goes anywhere. Build the first basket with the buyer in the room. An account left to place its own first order usually does not. Train the kitchen, not one person. An account that depends on a single individual disappears when that individual leaves. Go back in week two. Most restaurants stop between the first order and the second, and that gap is the whole job. Keep both sides transacting Watch behaviour on your accounts: how fast suppliers accept, whether quantities are confirmed honestly, whether prices are updated when they move, which buyers have gone quiet. Call the account the moment something slips and fix the cause. It is usually one untrained rep or a price list three weeks out of date. Keep catalogues current through the year: new items, delisted items, seasonal ranges, price changes. Prices move fast in this market and a stale catalogue costs trust on both sides of the order. Chase dormant accounts before the monthly numbers do it for you. An account you onboarded and lost is your account. Run the commercial housekeeping Prepare the monthly reconciliation for your supplier accounts, send it, and chase acceptance inside the agreed window. Track outstanding paperwork and commercial details on every account and close the gaps. Handle disputes with a clear head about where Cartify sits. You report what the platform recorded and help both sides reach a resolution. You do not arbitrate on quality, price or delivery, and you never take a position inside their commercial terms. Feed the platform Report catalogue and workflow problems in writing every week: item types the catalogue cannot hold, statuses that fire at the wrong moment, anything an account has to work around. Bring specifics. Account name, order number, screenshot. A general complaint cannot be fixed and will not be. Sit in the weekly review with your numbers ready: accounts onboarded, accounts live, catalogue items live and accurate, response times, accounts gone quiet. Who this suits Three to five years in food and beverage distribution, wholesale, hospitality operations, or account management on a B2B platform. Time inside a supplier's or a restaurant's own team counts for a lot here. You are comfortable with a spreadsheet of several thousand rows and can spot the twelve that are wrong. You can hold a firm line with an owner who wants his catalogue live today, and still be welcome in his office next month. Organised without being reminded. This is fifteen accounts moving at once, each with a different open item. Comfortable in a kitchen at 11am and a supplier's back office at 3pm. Arabic and English. French helps. Own transport

review_candidates.title: Site Reliability Engineer, Compute
review_candidates.description: About Fluidstack We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI. We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply! How We Operate Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role. Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible. Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins. Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward. Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world. The Production Engineering Team Examples of key exciting problems the team is working on Build the repair pipeline that keeps pace with a fleet of 10s to 100s of GWs: at our scale, a GPU failure isn't a ticket. It's a throughput problem. We're building the automation that takes a chip from fault detection through triage, RMA, and return to service without human intervention. Qualify every new GPU generation inside a 6-month build window: our platform covers burn-in, performance baselining, and NPI execution. It has to define "production-ready" before a site goes live, not after. New hardware gets certified at speeds unheard of in the industry. Migrate live compute at construction speed: we're converting clusters across production sites simultaneously, bringing new sites online, and making Kubernetes-orchestrated bare metal sustainable at the pace we're building – multiple GW annually. See and own the entire fleet in real time, at any scale: build the observability and orchestration layer that makes hyperscale AI compute actually operable. Debug, tune, and performance-test infrastructure that grows by another site every few months. Role Scope Own compute fleet health end to end. Build the metrics pipelines, alerting, and unified health view that tell you the true state of every GPU in production — across Kubernetes-orchestrated workloads and bare metal, at scale. Turn deployment/repair into a pipeline, not a procedure. Build and own the automation that takes a compute failure from detection through triage, parts management, and return to service. No one-off scripts, no heroics. Design and expand the GPU qualification platform. Burn-in, performance baselining, and NPI execution for every new GPU generation. You define what "good" looks like before hardware goes into production. Own Redfish and BMC tooling. Firmware-level telemetry, log collection at fleet scale, and the low-level access layer that repair automation and health tooling depend on. Own end-to-end reliability, scalability, and operation of the compute fleet at-scale. Fluidstack is building one of the largest GPU fleets in the world and that can only be accomplished with aggressive automation, tooling, and incident discipline. What We're Looking For The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would. You treat toil as a bug. Manual steps in a repair workflow are a backlog item, not a job description. You have an instinct for hardware. You're comfortable reasoning about failure modes at the firmware and silicon level, not just the software stack above it. You move toward ambiguity, not away from it. You walk into the fog, build the map, and explain it to everyone else. You learn at a steep slope. You reach real competence in an unfamiliar domain fast. We value this over existing expertise. You carry a pager without flinching. You run the incident, write the postmortem, fix the systemic cause, and move on. You're fluent with AI tooling. LLM APIs, MCP servers, and agentic frameworks, and you drive Claude Code, Cursor, or similar every day. You've shipped production automation that other teams depend on, and you're comfortable in any language using AI coding tools. Bonus: Hardware lifecycle management and RMA automation. BMC/Redfish or IPMI tooling. GPU qualification or burn-in frameworks. Workflow and orchestration engines (Temporal, Cadence). Metrics and alerting pipelines (Prometheus, Grafana). Go or Python... Salary & Benefits Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity). Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms. Health, dental, and vision insurance. Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms. Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units. We are committed to pay equity and transparency. Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch. Key Responsibilities Lead and implement Organizational Development and Organizational Effectiveness initiatives aligned with business and manufacturing objectives. Lead and continuously improve the Performance Management System, including KPIs and alignment of organizational, departmental, and individual objectives. Support organizational restructuring and continuous improvement initiatives. Minimum 5 years of solid experience in Organizational Development. Previous experience in a Managerial or Senior OD role is highly preferred. Manufacturing or Industrial experience is mandatory. Experience in the Cable Manufacturing Industry is highly preferred. Strong hands-on experience in: Organizational Design & Organizational Structure Organizational Effectiveness Job Analysis, Job Descriptions & Job Architecture Job Evaluation & Job Grading Performance Management & KPI Frameworks Competency Frameworks Career Paths Manpower & Workforce Planning HR Analytics & Reporting Experience with Job Master and Hay Group Job Evaluation Methodologies is highly preferred. Experience in conducting and analyzing Salary Surveys and Compensation Benchmarking is highly preferred. Strong analytical, leadership, communication, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills. Strong command of English, both written and spoken.

review_candidates.title: Office Coordinator
review_candidates.description: Company Description MIHAD Developments, headquartered in Al-Khamayel, El Sheikh Zayed City, is an emerging company delivering high-quality commercial projects through thoughtful planning, transparent operations, and a collaborative work environment. Role Description The Executive Secretary will provide comprehensive administrative and executive support to senior management in a full-time, on-site role based in Giza. Responsibilities include managing calendars, scheduling meetings, organizing travel arrangements, and preparing reports, presentations, and correspondence. The role involves handling incoming calls and emails, maintaining records and filing systems, and coordinating internal and external communication. The Executive Secretary will also support company secretarial tasks, assist with documentation for real estate projects, and ensure professional customer service to visitors and clients. This position requires careful attention to detail, discretion with confidential information, and the ability to prioritize tasks in a fast-paced environment. Requirements & Qualifications Professional Experience: 4+ years of experience in the same role or in similar executive administrative and secretarial positions, supporting senior leadership and managing confidential information. Clerical Skills: Strong administrative skills including document preparation, filing, data entry, and basic office administration. Technical Proficiency: Proficiency in office productivity software, including word processing, spreadsheets, email, and presentation tools. Communication & Customer Service: Excellent communication and customer service abilities, with a professional demeanor when dealing with internal and external stakeholders. Organization & Time Management: Solid organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to handle multiple tasks, meet deadlines, and maintain high attention to detail and accuracy in record-keeping. Qualifications: A diploma or bachelor’s degree in business administration, management, or a related field, with prior experience in real estate, construction, or a related sector considered an advantage.
